guard_streams.source: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider failure, contract transfer and consumer-support guidance do not establish current fixed-broadband coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider-failure guidance on 13 February 2026.
Where another company takes over, service should usually continue without interruption.
The existing contract should normally transfer to the new provider.
If the new provider changes contract terms, the customer should be able to exit without an early termination charge.
Customers unhappy with the replacement provider can switch to another provider.
Switching during a minimum contract period can otherwise involve early termination charges.
Ofcom points customers to price-comparison websites to compare replacement deals.
If no company takes over, the service will stop on a date the failed provider should communicate.
Customers should not pay an early termination charge, but keeping the current phone number may not be possible.
Providers should offer good customer care and may provide additional support to vulnerable customers.

guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: Supplier-declared existing and planned build, consultation status and regional outputs require exact current-status and parcel-identity validation before any coverage promotion.

facts.detail: BDUK published the January 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review on 6 January 2026.
The consultation page was last updated on 10 June 2026.
The January 2026 consultation is concluded.
The outcome records the formal close and outlines next steps.
The request invited all suppliers to submit existing and planned build information at premises level.
The information request covers the next three years across the UK.
The consultation ran from 3pm on 6 January to 5pm on 6 February 2026.
The review seeks to confirm where gigabit-capable infrastructure currently exists or is planned.
BDUK states that the National Rolling OMR occurs in January, May and September.
The 10 June update added a link to regional outputs in the closure notice.
